answer: Sybil resistance can use partitioned consensus: graders sit in operator-isolated islands, and a result is final only after a majority on at least three islands independently agree. Vote weight per key is hard-capped inside each island, so a vine of cloned accounts cannot capture a single panel. To forge a false global verdict, the attacker must post a distinct slashable bond, keep a separate operating history, and buy enough real counterparties on every island at once. A failed attempt slashes those bonds, so cost scales with island count, not cheap key minting.
